text:
Taylor (customer): hey team, private installer in our VPC is failing to pull model shards and pip deps after we enabled corporate proxy. getting 403 on some hosts and TLS handshake failures on others. can you advise? :wave:
Chris (support): hey Taylor — sorry for the hit. can you paste the curl + error you see and the env (k8s/VM) ? also is TLS intercept enabled in the proxy?
Taylor (customer): k8s on EKS, using our egress proxy. here's the curl we run from the pod: `curl -v https://model-registry.redwood-internal.com/api/v1/shards/abc -o /dev/null`
Taylor (customer): response: `* About to connect() to model-registry.redwood-internal.com port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to model-registry.redwood-internal.com:443
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to model-registry.redwood-internal.com:443`
Taylor (customer): also for pypi: `curl -v https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/requests/` returns `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`
Chris (support): thanks. two things likely: (1) proxy is blocking/rewriting SNI or not allowing those hostnames, (2) TLS intercept may be replacing certs and pod doesn't trust intercept CA. can you run `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood-internal.com:443 -servername model-registry.redwood-internal.com -showcerts` from the pod and paste first 5 lines?
Taylor (customer): output snip: `CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = DigiCert, OU = www.digicert.com, CN = DigiCert Global Root G2
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
---
Certificate chain`
Taylor (customer): so proxy is injecting their cert. we can't add their CA to pods easily. any minimal hosts we can request open to bypass proxy?
Riya (sre): short answer: you need outbound allowlist entries for the package repos, model registry, auth, telemetry, and OCSP endpoints. also allowlist CDN/ip ranges used by our model shard CDN. if TLS intercept is mandatory you must add the proxy CA to your cluster trust store or use egress rules to bypass TLS inspection for these FQDNs.
Riya (sre): proposed minimal FQDN allowlist (TCP 443):
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- packaging.python.org
- artifactory.redwood.com
- model-registry.redwood-internal.com
- auth.redwood.example.com
- telemetry.redwood.example.com
- models-cdn.redwood-cdn.net
- s3.amazonaws.com (or specific S3 bucket host)
- ocsp.digicert.com
- crl3.digicert.com
- time.cloudflare.com (for TLS client time checks)
Riya (sre): note: if you use Fastly/Cloudflare for CDN there may be many edge IPs; allow by FQDN + 443 is preferable.
Chris (support): adding: ports 443 outbound required, and allow DNS to resolve these FQDNs without split-horizon rewriting. if your split-horizon DNS rewrites model-registry to an internal ip, ensure the internal ip is reachable and cert valid (SNI match).
DevEx: FYI — installer also calls `registries.redwood-internal.com` for model signatures and `kms.redwood-int.example.com` for key exchange. please add those as well if you use private registry.
Taylor (customer): thanks — could you give a one-liner we can hand to networking? they want a tidy list.
Riya (sre): sure — paste below. you can hand them this exact block:
````
Allow outbound HTTPS (TCP/443) to these FQDNs (no TLS interception or add proxy CA to trust store):
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- packaging.python.org
- artifactory.redwood.com
- model-registry.redwood-internal.com
- registries.redwood-internal.com
- auth.redwood.example.com
- telemetry.redwood.example.com
- models-cdn.redwood-cdn.net
- s3.amazonaws.com (or specific bucket host)
- ocsp.digicert.com
- crl3.digicert.com
- kms.redwood-int.example.com
Notes:
- Ensure SNI is preserved by the proxy. If the proxy performs TLS intercept, add the proxy's CA cert to the cluster node/pod trust store or configure an egress rule to bypass interception for the listed domains.
- DNS must resolve the public FQDNs correctly (no transparent split-horizon that returns internal IPs unless internal service is properly certed).
````
Taylor (customer): handing to network now. one more: for repro we saw 403 only for files.pythonhosted.org — any quick test we can run to prove it's proxy rule?
Chris (support): run: `curl -vI --resolve files.pythonhosted.org:443:<your-proxy-ip> https://files.pythonhosted.org/` — if you get 403 from proxy, it's on the proxy. also try `curl -vk https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/requests/` to see cert chain.
Taylor (customer): ran both — `--resolve` still returned 403, `-k` shows proxy cert. so proxy is doing hostname based allow/block.
Riya (sre): okay that matches. network will need to add rules to allow files.pythonhosted.org and packaging.python.org. alternatively they can allow GitHub raw assets and pypi CDNs.
Chris (support): we'll open an internal ticket to track this from our side too. assigning to InfraBot to log case and follow up with networking contact. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: case created: RNW-6152. assignee: network-team. note: requested allowlist + guidance provided.
Taylor (customer): thanks all — will update once network confirms. :pray:
